learningObjective: Understand how StableHLO represents dynamic shapes and identify true statements about StableHLO's design intent regarding portability and shape.

canonicalClaims.claim: StableHLO is a portable, framework-independent op set that supports both static and dynamic tensor shapes (with optional per-dim bounds), and is designed to be consumed by multiple compiler backends.
conditions: The framework emits StableHLO consistent with the spec's op signatures.
nonImplications: Does not imply every backend implements every StableHLO op; portability is at the spec level.
Does not imply StableHLO includes runtime/device concerns; those live in downstream layers.

sourceMappings.locator: StableHLO spec: portability and dynamic shape

canonicalClaims.claim: StableHLO permits dynamic shape via `?` dims and optional bounds encoded on the tensor type; static and dynamic-shape programs coexist in the spec.
conditions: The IR uses the specified dynamic shape syntax.
nonImplications: Does not imply dynamic-shape programs are always as fast as specialized-shape programs.

misconceptions.claim: StableHLO requires all shapes to be static.
StableHLO is a runtime that executes the graph directly.
misconceptions.whyWrong: StableHLO is an IR/interchange format; execution is by downstream compilers/runtimes.

misconceptions.claim: StableHLO ops carry device placement and stream scheduling attributes.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Device/stream/runtime concerns are not part of the StableHLO op set.

misconceptions.claim: StableHLO is specific to Google TPUs and cannot target GPU/CPU backends.
misconceptions.whyWrong: StableHLO is a portable IR; XLA and other compilers target CPU/GPU/TPU from StableHLO.

implementationFacts: StableHLO ops carry per-value shape/dtype annotations
Dynamic dims are written as `?`; bounds attributes are optional per dim
Consumers include XLA compilers (CPU/GPU/TPU) and IREE
performanceScenarios: Backends specialize dynamic-shape programs to concrete shapes when profitable; the IR permits both modes.
